entries.title: Star Wars Episode IX: The Rise of Skywalker

violence.summary: Heavy sci-fi action includes space battles, shoot-outs, crashes, lightsaber combat, mass casualties, explicit but mostly bloodless deaths, creepy creatures, a grotesque preserved villain, and emotionally significant character losses.

language.summary: Infrequent mild swearing and insults include words such as ass, hell, damn, stupid, and fantasy-specific put-downs.

romance.summary: Romance is limited to charged looks, hugs, brief kisses, and a supernatural bond with romantic undertones.

drinking.summary: A backstory reference to being a spice runner carries a drug-running implication.

handoffNotes: Several deaths of primary and supporting characters may need emotional-content prose.
CSM notes flashing-light sequences that may be relevant outside the four content flags.

entries.title: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story

violence.summary: War violence is unusually heavy for the franchise, with many major and minor deaths, shoot-outs, Death Star destruction, dead bodies, a child witnessing parental loss, and a mind-invasion torture scene.

language.summary: Language is limited to hostile labels such as traitor, thief, and criminal.

romance.summary: Two leads show attraction through longing looks, close conversation, and one climactic embrace.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: The high body count and sacrifice-centered ending may need emotional-content prose.

entries.title: Solo: A Star Wars Story

violence.summary: Sci-fi action includes warfare, executions, shoot-outs, decapitation, duels, chases, crashes, frequent peril, implied torture, and deaths of more than one supporting character.

language.summary: Language includes one cut-off stronger exclamation plus mild profanity and insults.

romance.summary: Several kisses and embraces appear, and one major character is consistently flirtatious.

drinking.summary: Some scenes take place in pubs with drinking and gambling, and one captain drinks from a flask during battle.

entries.title: Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu

language.summary: Language is limited to a quick hell and threatening talk.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface sex, romance, or nudity content.

drinking.summary: Cantina and bar scenes show apparent alcohol, gas is used to incapacitate a character, a poisonous bite is discussed, and a Hutt smokes an unknown substance.

handoffNotes: This is a future-dated 2026 entry, but the catalog srcUrl currently resolves to a full CSM page.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets

violence.summary: Fantasy peril includes giant spiders, a deadly basilisk, comatose-looking victims, a tense climax, Harry's broken and boneless arm, self-punishment by a house elf, a threatening snake, a flying-car near fall, and gross-out slug vomiting.

language.summary: The main language concern is Draco using an offensive wizarding-world slur against Hermione.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface sex, romance, or nudity content.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: Sensitive kids may need prose around repeated child peril and scary creature imagery.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban

violence.summary: Darker magical peril includes Dementor attacks, a soul-removal threat, Harry hearing his mother's death, a provoked hippogriff injury, an offscreen execution setup, fear-shifting boggarts, Ron's broken leg, murder threats, and a werewolf chase.

language.summary: A few mild British swears and one damn are noted.

romance.summary: Romance is limited to teen flirting.

drinking.summary: Butterbeer is introduced as a lightly alcoholic magical-world drink, and kids visit a pub.

handoffNotes: Harry repeatedly hearing his mother's death during Dementor attacks may need emotional-content prose.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire

violence.summary: The fourth film includes two deaths, one sad teen death, lifeless bodies, dragon attacks, underwater peril, a tortured spider, a severed hand used in ritual magic, and Harry writhing under a torture curse.

language.summary: Mild British slang and phrases such as piss off are noted.

romance.summary: Romance grows with the teens: sexual-interest references, a ghost entering Harry's bath, and shadowy post-dance kissing.

drinking.summary: Magical horses drink single-malt whiskey, and students drink butterbeer.

handoffNotes: CSM specifically flags the teen death and separation/anxiety themes as potentially upsetting.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix

violence.summary: Intense magical danger includes Dementors, Death Eaters, Voldemort, centaurs dragging off a character, torture-like school punishment, a bloody snake attack, a frightening climactic battle, a key death, and Harry being painfully possessed.

language.summary: CSM notes one mild British swear.

romance.summary: Harry and Cho kiss, while Ron and Hermione continue flirtatious bickering and glances.

drinking.summary: Harry and friends meet in a rundown pub but do not drink.

handoffNotes: The upsetting death of someone close to Harry and his anger/grief afterward may need emotional-content prose.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince

violence.summary: Dark fantasy danger includes a beloved character's death, a severe bloody curse wound, bruising and beating, poisonings, a life-threatening seizure, Death Eater attacks, a kidnapping, and frightening skeleton-like creatures.

language.summary: Mild insults, British slang, and a couple of religious exclamations are noted.

romance.summary: Teen romance is more prominent, with flirting, kissing, hallway make-outs, attraction talk, jealousy, hand-holding, love potions, and breakups.

drinking.summary: Underage characters drink butterbeer, mead, and wine-like drinks; a professor serves alcohol to teens, adults drink heavily, and magical potions affect behavior.

handoffNotes: Beloved-character death and sorrow are central enough to need emotional-content prose.
Drinking detail is stronger than the simple a little label may suggest because adults serve teens alcohol.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows - Part 1

violence.summary: This installment has many deaths, including recurring characters, a bloody knife death, torture, severe injury, near drowning, a bloody ear wound, mistreatment of targeted people, Death Eaters and Dementors, and a snake bursting from a corpse.

language.summary: Language includes repeated British slang, mild profanity, religious exclamations, and repeated wizarding-world slurs.

romance.summary: Romance includes Harry and Ginny kissing after a dress-zip scene, longing looks and embraces, and a tormenting vision where Harry and Hermione appear nearly nude while kissing.

drinking.summary: Champagne appears at a wedding reception and goblets are on a dinner table, but CSM says no meaningful drinking is shown.

handoffNotes: High body count, torture, grief, and a beloved character death need emotional-content prose.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows - Part 2

violence.summary: The finale is the deadliest Potter film, with the Battle of Hogwarts, hundreds of implied deaths, bodies of beloved characters, bloody goblin deaths, Killing Curses, a gory snake attack, fire peril, disintegration, a disturbing body remnant, and Harry willingly facing death.

language.summary: Language includes one stronger insult in a famous line plus mild British slang.

romance.summary: Ron and Hermione kiss, hold hands, embrace, and comfort each other; Harry and Ginny briefly kiss, and another character talks about declaring romantic feelings before battle.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: The battle deaths, visible bodies, Harry's sacrifice, and grief-heavy finale need emotional-content prose.

entries.title: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them

violence.summary: Darker adult-centered fantasy includes mass destruction, gruesome deaths, wand battles, near execution in an acid-like pool, uncontrolled magic threatening Manhattan, and child abuse with visible welts and cuts.

language.summary: Language includes mild fantasy exclamations, mild swearing, insults, and one anatomical term.

romance.summary: A woman changes clothes around men and is ogled, later appears in nightwear, makes a mild sexual allusion, and couples kiss, hold, or stare longingly.

drinking.summary: Adults order drinks in a speakeasy, a magical alcoholic drink is implied, and a supporting character smokes a cigar.

handoffNotes: Child abuse and visible injury may need prose separate from general fantasy violence.

entries.title: Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald

violence.summary: The sequel has a high body count, injuries, mass destruction, wand battles, attacks on adults and children, deaths from creatures, curses, drowning, magical fire, executions, and destructive transformations.

language.summary: Insults and a couple of mild swear words are noted.

romance.summary: Couples kiss, hug, cuddle, and exchange longing looks; one scene has a man resting his head on a woman's chest, and a flashback shows teen flirtation.

drinking.summary: Queenie serves bottled drinks that look like beer or butterbeer.

handoffNotes: CSM's violence detail also mentions an implied coercive sexual relationship, which may need prose despite the romance label staying a little.

entries.title: The Great Muppet Caper

violence.summary: Slapstick includes characters thrown from vehicles, Gonzo repeatedly falling into traffic, Miss Piggy tossing and karate-chopping people, comic electrocution, a gun threat, a cab crash, and talk that someone could be killed during a heist.

language.summary: A song includes one mild hell reference.

romance.summary: Kermit and Miss Piggy kiss, another character tries to kiss Miss Piggy, and there is adult-aimed innuendo involving models, a dressing room, bikinis, unwanted touching, and an affair reference.

entries.title: A Christmas Story

violence.summary: Bullying includes arm-twisting and a black eye; Ralphie punches a bully bloody, a BB-gun fantasy kills comic bandits, a child's tongue freezes to a pole, a dog's ear is caught in a door, children face physical punishment, and a scary Santa slide sequence appears.

language.summary: Kids and adults use or discuss stronger language, including ass, son of a bitch, hell, hot damn, insults, frequent offscreen-style adult swearing, and Ralphie's famous censored F-word moment followed by soap punishment.

romance.summary: Sexual humor centers on the leg lamp and a mild blue-balls joke after a bowling ball lands in a man's lap.

drinking.summary: Ralphie's parents drink wine after opening presents, and his father offers Ralphie a sip that his mother declines for him.

handoffNotes: CSM also flags racist stereotypes in the Chinese restaurant scene and other period racism; this sits outside the requested four flags but should be considered by reviewers.
